body:
DETERMINATION: The observation-cursor behaviour that applies to this workspace's Ordarium integration is a **single, global, filter-independent durable commit position** over the whole ledger — NOT a per-subscription position.

WHICH INTEGRATION
- This workspace is the Palimpsest DSH plugin. Its Ordarium integration is the pinned release-tarball line: `package.json` pins `@ordarium/core`, `@ordarium/host-kit`, `@ordarium/ledger-sqlite` (runtime) and `@ordarium/testing` (dev) to `ordarium-v1.3.1`; `pnpm-workspace.yaml` `overrides:` repeat the same four 1.3.1 tarball URLs; installed artifacts are `node_modules/@ordarium/core@1.3.1`, `ledger-sqlite@1.3.1`, `host-kit@1.3.1`. So "the exact pinned version" = Ordarium 1.3.1.

THE APPARENT CONFLICT, AND WHY IT RESOLVES LOCALLY
- The only in-repo source that speaks to cursor scope is `docs/engineering/notes/cursor-note.md`, which claims positions are "per-subscription, not global". It self-declares: "Status: informational, not normative" and "was not updated against the current pinned artifact". No other repo document (including the cross-repo charter `07-ordarium-alignment.md` and the normative `03-system-design-spec.md`) contains any cursor provision.
- `docs/engineering/08-source-precedence-policy.md` (PLMP-ALN-2) supplies an explicit, co-applicable order: (1) the published contract of the exact pinned version — its shipped type declarations and release specification — governs that interface's behaviour; (2) the project normative spec (PLMP-SDS, `03`) governs project-internal semantics; (3) informational records (engineering notes, historical alignment records, release commentaries) are explanatory only and never override 1 or 2; (4) an explicitly superseded source is void.
- The cursor-scope question is an Ordarium interface behaviour, so tier 1 governs, not tier 2. The note is tier 3 and also temporally scoped to "an earlier Ordarium line". Therefore tier 3 yields to tier 1; the conflict is not genuine.

WHAT THE PINNED 1.3.1 CONTRACT AND IMPLEMENTATION SAY (tier 1)
- `node_modules/@ordarium/core/dist/src/types.d.ts`, `StateChangePage` (ORD-BOOT-0): `cursor` is an "Opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change", always present (unlike `nextCursor?` on other read surfaces) so a consumer at the end of the feed still holds a durable resume position; `StateChangeFeed.changes(filter?, cursor?)`; `StateChangeFilter` carries only `namespace`/`limit`; `LedgerCapabilities.stateChangeFeed?` gates the capability, and `supportsStateChangeFeed` is the fail-closed entry.
- `state.d.ts`: `OrdariumStateStore.changes` delegates to that feed; a ledger lacking the capability fails closed with LEDGER_CAPABILITY_REQUIRED.
- `errors.d.ts`, `InvalidCursorError`: a caller-supplied change-feed cursor that "could not be decoded as a durable position" is invalid *input* (distinct from LEDGER_CORRUPT) and fails closed "instead of silently restarting from the beginning of the feed".
- `@ordarium/ledger-sqlite@1.3.1` `SqliteLedger.changes`: positions come from a global `ordarium_state_changes` `change_seq` ordering row written in the same transaction as the CAS revision; the decoded cursor is validated against the ledger-wide high-water mark — "the cursor is a global, filter-independent position, so this compares against the whole ledger, not the requested namespace's last sequence"; a position above the high-water mark throws `InvalidCursorError` (restored/replaced ledger); `namespace` is applied only as a WHERE-narrowing after the position filter.
- `@ordarium/core@1.3.1` `MemoryLedger.changes`: same semantics — positions are contiguous 1..n over the whole ledger, the namespace filter is applied by `continue`(ing) non-matching entries while the returned cursor remains the global position.

CONSEQUENCE FOR CONSUMERS
- One cursor value is meaningful across differently filtered feeds: a cursor obtained from an unfiltered `changes()` call can be reused on a `namespace`-filtered call and vice versa; filtering narrows which records are delivered but never renumbers or rewinds the position.
- The position is monotonic (concurrent commits only raise the high-water mark), so a valid cursor cannot be spuriously rejected by later commits; a position beyond the high-water mark (foreign/restored/replaced ledger) fails closed with `InvalidCursorError` rather than silently restarting at 0.
- This is a contract-level determination for any future consumption. The workspace does not currently consume the observation cursor: grep finds 0 hits for `StateChangeFeed`/`stateChangeFeed`/`.changes(` in `src`, `test` and `docs`. The one state-kind consumer, `src/telemetry/state_persistence.ts`, uses `OrdariumStateStore.list` (cursor pagination on the `listStates` surface) plus revision-CAS writes, not the change feed.

PERIPHERAL NOTE
- `07-ordarium-alignment.md`'s latest registered revision (r19) still names a 1.2.0 baseline, a documentation lag versus the actual 1.3.1 pin. That lag does not create a cursor-scope conflict (07 contains no cursor provision), and informational/historical records cannot override the pinned artifact under rule 1 vs rule 3. Reaching the exact pinned artifact's shipped declarations and implementations was sufficient; no cross-repo authority gap remained, so no peer contact was warranted.
